name: Jellyfin Federation
description: Aggregate content from multiple Jellyfin servers into unified virtual libraries
overview: The Jellyfin Federation Plugin allows you to create a unified media library by aggregating content from multiple remote Jellyfin servers. Stream content from any server without file synchronization.
changelog:
Adds a second credential tier for streaming, on top of 0.0.70's federation token. The federation token proves "this request is from friend X" and covers browsing/admin-ish calls - it was never meant to authorize streaming alone, and never has: DirectStream/image gateway calls already required a separate, short-lived token minted per item. That per-item token only ever knew "this item was requested", not which of the friend's own users was actually watching, so a per-remote-user restriction could only be enforced from a self-reported header at browse time, not at the moment streaming is actually granted.

Now, the moment one of a friend's users actually starts playing something, their server registers that specific user and gets back a session token scoped to them - checked against your per-remote-user rules right then (a fully blocked user never gets a session token at all), and re-checked per item on every single stream request after that. Falls back automatically to the old per-item token for a friend still on an older version, so nothing breaks for anyone not yet updated.

214 tests (up from 210).
